sections.title: 1. First Meetings, Office Bearers & Objectives Resolution

masteryZone.q: Who was elected as the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly in its first meeting?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, being the oldest member, was elected temporary President following French practice.

masteryZone.q: Who were the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: The Assembly had two Vice-Presidents: H.C. Mookerjee and V.T. Krishnamachari.

masteryZone.q: Who was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: Sir B.N. Rau was appointed as the Legal/Constitutional Advisor to the Assembly.

masteryZone.q: Jawaharlal Nehru introduced the historic 'Objectives Resolution' on:
masteryZone.sol: The Objectives Resolution was introduced by Nehru on December 13, 1946.

masteryZone.q: The Objectives Resolution was unanimously adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
masteryZone.sol: The Objectives Resolution was adopted unanimously on January 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly? (Select all that apply)
opts: It was boycotted by the Muslim League.
Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha presided over it.
masteryZone.sol: The first meeting was on Dec 9, 1946, boycotted by the League, attended by only 211 members, and presided by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha.

masteryZone.q: Who among the following were office-bearers of the Constituent Assembly? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was President; H.C. Mookerjee and V.T. Krishnamachari were Vice-Presidents; Sir B.N. Rau was Legal Advisor.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following values were declared in the Objectives Resolution? (Select all that apply)
opts: India as an independent sovereign republic
Guaranteed social, economic, and political justice
Adequate safeguards for minorities and tribal areas
masteryZone.sol: The resolution declared India a sovereign republic, guaranteed justice/equality, and safeguarded minorities. It did not support constitutional monarchy.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are true about the transition of the Objectives Resolution? (Select all that apply)
opts: It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.
Its modified version forms the Preamble of the present Constitution.
It was rejected by the princely states.
masteryZone.sol: Moved by Nehru, adopted on Jan 22, 1947, and modified into the Preamble. It was not rejected by the states.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following administrative staff roles are correctly matched? (Select all that apply)
opts: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar - Secretary to Assembly
masteryZone.sol: Iengar was Secretary, Mukerjee was Chief Draftsman, Rau was Advisor. Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

masteryZone.q: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected temporary President of the Constituent Assembly on December 9, 1946.
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected temporary President. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on Dec 11.

masteryZone.q: The French practice of electing the oldest member was followed to choose the temporary President.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was chosen following the French practice.

masteryZone.q: The Muslim League fully participated in the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: The Muslim League boycotted the first meeting, demanding Pakistan.

masteryZone.q: The Constituent Assembly had two Vice-Presidents.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, it had two Vice-Presidents: H.C. Mookerjee and V.T. Krishnamachari.

masteryZone.q: The Objectives Resolution was moved by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
masteryZone.sol: It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.

masteryZone.q: The Objectives Resolution was adopted on the same day it was introduced.
masteryZone.sol: No, it was introduced on Dec 13, 1946, and adopted on Jan 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: Sir B.N. Rau was a member of the Drafting Committee.
masteryZone.sol: No, he was the Legal/Constitutional Advisor, not a member of the Drafting Committee.

masteryZone.q: Only 211 members attended the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, due to the boycott by the Muslim League.

masteryZone.q: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on December 9, _______.
masteryZone.sol: It met first on December 9, 1946.

masteryZone.q: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected as the _______ President of the Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: He was the temporary President.

masteryZone.q: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as permanent President on December _______, 1946.
masteryZone.sol: He was elected permanent President on Dec 11, 1946.

masteryZone.q: The Assembly appointed Sir B.N. _______ as its Constitutional Advisor.
masteryZone.sol: Sir B.N. Rau was the Legal Advisor.

masteryZone.q: The Objectives Resolution was moved in the Assembly by Jawaharlal _______.
masteryZone.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru moved it on Dec 13, 1946.

masteryZone.q: The Objectives Resolution was adopted by the Assembly on January 22, _______.
masteryZone.sol: It was adopted on January 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble is the modified version of the _______ Resolution.
masteryZone.sol: It is modified from the Objectives Resolution.

masteryZone.q: The French practice was followed to elect the oldest member, Dr. Sachchidananda _______, as temporary President.
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected temporary President.

options.text: A. Permanent President of the Assembly

options.text: A. First meeting and election of temporary President
B. Introduction of the Objectives Resolution by Nehru

masteryZone.sol: Options match directly (I-A, II-B, III-C).

masteryZone.q: Who presided over the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (as temporary President).

masteryZone.q: Which political group boycotted the first session of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: The Muslim League.

masteryZone.q: Why did Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha preside over the first session instead of Dr. Rajendra Prasad?
masteryZone.sol: Because Dr. Prasad had not yet been elected permanent President; Sinha was chosen as the oldest member under French practice.

masteryZone.q: Name the two individuals who served as Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: H.C. Mookerjee and V.T. Krishnamachari.

masteryZone.q: Who moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru.

masteryZone.q: What was the date of the adoption of the Objectives Resolution?
masteryZone.sol: January 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: Which constitutional advisor drafted the first draft of the Indian Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Sir B.N. Rau.

masteryZone.q: How many members attended the first session of the assembly on December 9, 1946?
masteryZone.sol: 211 members.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the office-bearers of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the permanent President.
2. V.T. Krishnamachari was the sole Vice-President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because there were two Vice-Presidents (H.C. Mookerjee and V.T. Krishnamachari).

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Objectives Resolution was moved by Nehru on December 13, 1946.
2. It was adopted unanimously on January 22, 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The temporary President of the Assembly was selected using British parliamentary conventions.
2. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected temporary President on December 9, 1946.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because the French practice (not British) of selecting the oldest member was followed.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sir B.N. Rau was the legal advisor who prepared the first draft of the constitution.
2. H.V.R. Iengar was the Secretary of the Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, describing B.N. Rau and H.V.R. Iengar's roles.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Objectives Resolution:
1. It declared India as an independent sovereign republic.
2. It specified that all power and authority of sovereign India are derived from the British Crown.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because it declared that all power and authority of independent India are derived from the people, not the Crown.

masteryZone.q: Why did the first session of the Constituent Assembly have such low attendance (211 members)?
masteryZone.sol: Because the Muslim League boycotted the assembly's proceedings, refusing to participate in constitution-making for a united India and insisting on their demand for a separate state of Pakistan.

masteryZone.q: Why was Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha elected as the temporary President of the Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: To establish an immediate presiding officer for the opening session before the permanent elections could be conducted. Following the French practice, Sinha was chosen because he was the oldest member of the assembly.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Objectives Resolution considered the foundation of the Indian Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Because it laid down the fundamental philosophy, core values (justice, liberty, equality, fraternity), and structural principles of the future Indian polity. Its ideals directly guided the drafting and shaped the Preamble.

masteryZone.q: How was the leadership of the Constituent Assembly structured?
masteryZone.sol: It was headed by a permanent President (Dr. Rajendra Prasad) and assisted by two Vice-Presidents (H.C. Mookerjee representing British provinces, and V.T. Krishnamachari representing princely states) along with a Constitutional Advisor (Sir B.N. Rau).

masteryZone.q: How did the French practice influence the first day of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: It provided a clear precedent for choosing a temporary president: electing the oldest member of the House (Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha) to preside over the initial meetings and lead the election of the permanent president.

masteryZone.q: How did the Objectives Resolution eventually influence the present Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: It was adopted unanimously, acted as the framework for all drafting committees, and was later modified to become the Preamble of the Constitution, serving as the interpretative key to all constitutional provisions.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: During the opening session on December 9, 1946, the Muslim League seats remained vacant. How did this boycott affect the assembly's legal legitimacy to frame a constitution for the entire country under the Cabinet Mission plan?
masteryZone.sol: It created a political deadlock. Winston Churchill likened it to 'a marriage where the bride is absent'. However, the assembly proceeded with its work, and the legal status was eventually resolved by the Indian Independence Act of 1947, which formally partitioned British India and made the assembly fully sovereign for the Indian dominion.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: On December 11, 1946, the assembly met to elect its permanent President. Dr. Rajendra Prasad's name was proposed. Why was a permanent election necessary immediately after Dr. Sinha had been selected on December 9?
masteryZone.sol: Because Dr. Sinha was only a temporary President chosen under the French practice to lead the first day's proceedings. To conduct formal, long-term constitution-making and maintain institutional stability, a permanent President elected by the members was essential.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: A debate arose in late December 1946 on whether to adopt the Objectives Resolution immediately. Some members argued that the assembly should wait for the Muslim League and princely states to join. How was this debate resolved?
masteryZone.sol: The assembly decided to postpone the adoption of the resolution to give time for the absent members to join. It was eventually adopted unanimously on January 22, 1947, after it became clear that the Muslim League would not participate.

masteryZone.q: Explain the role and significance of Sir B.N. Rau in the Constituent Assembly to a beginner.
masteryZone.sol: Sir B.N. Rau was the Constitutional/Legal Advisor to the assembly. He did not draft the final constitution but prepared the initial draft based on his study of other world constitutions, which served as the raw material for Dr. B. Ambedkar's Drafting Committee.

masteryZone.q: Explain the meaning and components of the Objectives Resolution.
masteryZone.sol: The Objectives Resolution was a document moved by Nehru that declared: 1. India will be an independent sovereign republic. 2. All power comes from the people. 3. Citizens will have justice, equality, and freedom. 4. Minorities and tribal areas will be safeguarded. It set the blueprint for the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Explain the difference between the temporary and permanent President of the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: The temporary President (Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha) was selected on day one because he was the oldest member, following French practice, to administer the oath and run the initial meeting. The permanent President (Dr. Rajendra Prasad) was formally elected by the members on day three to lead the entire drafting process over the next three years.

sections.title: 2. Major Committees, Other Functions & Final Adoption

masteryZone.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, setup on August 29, 1947.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following committees was headed by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel?
masteryZone.sol: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the Chairman of the Provincial Constitution Committee.

masteryZone.q: When did the Constituent Assembly adopt the National Flag of India?
masteryZone.sol: The National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on July 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: How much time did the Constituent Assembly take to draft the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: The Assembly took exactly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to complete the task.

masteryZone.q: Who was the calligrapher of the original English version of the Indian Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Prem Behari Narain Raizada handwritten calligraphed the original English copy in a flowing italic style.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following Major Committees were chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Powers, Union Constitution, and States committees. Sardar Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following functions were performed by the Constituent Assembly on January 24, 1950? (Select all that apply)
opts: Election of Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India
masteryZone.sol: National Anthem, Song, and the first President were adopted/elected on Jan 24, 1950. The National Flag was adopted on July 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following statements are true about the Drafting Committee? (Select all that apply)
opts: It was set up on August 29, 1947.
It was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
masteryZone.sol: Set up on Aug 29, 1947 with 7 members under Ambedkar. It was the most important Major Committee, not a minor one.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following artists from Shantiniketan were involved in decorating the original Constitution? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Nandlal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha decorated and illuminated the pages. Abanindranath Tagore and Raja Ravi Varma were not involved.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following statistics regarding the making of the Constitution are correct? (Select all that apply)
opts: The makers studied constitutions of about 60 countries.
The total expenditure was Rs. 64 lakh.
The draft was considered for 200 days.
masteryZone.sol: It held 11 sessions, studied about 60 constitutions, and spent Rs. 64 lakh. The draft was considered for 114 days (not 200).

masteryZone.q: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel chaired the Union Powers Committee.
masteryZone.sol: No, Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee.

masteryZone.q: The National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly after India gained independence.
masteryZone.sol: The National Flag was adopted on July 22, 1947, which was before Independence (August 15, 1947).

masteryZone.q: Pingali Venkayya is credited with designing the National Flag of India.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, Pingali Venkayya designed the flag adopted by the assembly.

masteryZone.q: The National Anthem and National Song were both adopted on January 24, 1950.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, both were adopted on January 24, 1950.

masteryZone.q: The Constituent Assembly spent around Rs. 64 lakh in drafting the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, the total expenditure was Rs. 64 lakh.

masteryZone.q: H.V.R. Iengar calligraphed the original copy of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: Prem Behari Narain Raizada calligraphed the English version, and Vasant Krishan Vaidya calligraphed the Hindi version. Iengar was the Secretary.

masteryZone.q: The Elephant was adopted as the symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, the Elephant was the official seal/symbol of the assembly.

masteryZone.q: The draft constitution was considered by the assembly for exactly 114 days.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, the draft was discussed for 114 days.

masteryZone.q: The Drafting Committee was set up on August _______, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: It was set up on August 29, 1947.

masteryZone.q: The Drafting Committee consisted of _______ members.
masteryZone.sol: It had seven members: Ambedkar (Chairman), Ayyangar, Ayyar, Munshi, Sadullah, Madhava Rau, and Krishnamachari.

masteryZone.q: The National Flag was adopted on July 22, _______.
masteryZone.sol: It was adopted on July 22, 1947.

masteryZone.q: The National Anthem was adopted on January _______, 1950.
masteryZone.sol: It was adopted on January 24, 1950.

masteryZone.q: The making of the Constitution cost a total of Rs. _______ lakh.
masteryZone.sol: It cost Rs. 64 lakh.

masteryZone.q: The original English copy of the Constitution was calligraphed by Prem Behari Narain _______.
masteryZone.sol: Prem Behari Narain Raizada calligraphed the original copy.

masteryZone.q: The original Hindi version of the Constitution was calligraphed by Vasant Krishan _______.
masteryZone.sol: Vasant Krishan Vaidya calligraphed the Hindi version.

masteryZone.q: The design and illumination of the Preamble page was done by Beohar Rammanohar _______.
masteryZone.sol: Beohar Rammanohar Sinha decorated the Preamble page.

masteryZone.q: Match the committees of the Constituent Assembly with their Chairmen:
masteryZone.sol: Options match directly (I-A, II-B, III-C).

masteryZone.q: Match the calligraphers and artists with their contributions:

options.text: A. Calligrapher of the original English version

masteryZone.q: Who was the Chairman of the Provincial Constitution Committee?
masteryZone.sol: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

masteryZone.q: Name the designer of the National Flag of India.
masteryZone.sol: Pingali Venkayya.

masteryZone.q: How many members did the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly have?
masteryZone.sol: Seven members.

masteryZone.q: Which government body did the Constituent Assembly transform into on January 26, 1950?
masteryZone.sol: The Provisional Parliament of India.

masteryZone.q: What was the symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly?

masteryZone.q: Which artist from Shantiniketan decorated the Preamble page of the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Beohar Rammanohar Sinha.

1. Prem Behari Narain Raizada wrote the English version in italic handwriting.
2. Raizada charged Rs. 10,000 as his calligrapher fee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because Raizada did not charge any fee, requesting only to write his name on every page and his grandfather's name on the last page.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pingali Venkayya designed the National Flag adopted in 1947.
2. pingali Venkayya was from Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the final details:
1. Out of 299 members, 284 signed the Constitution on November 26, 1949.
2. The Constituent Assembly held its final session on January 26, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the final session was held on January 24, 1950 (not Jan 26).

masteryZone.q: Why did the Constituent Assembly appoint committees like the Drafting Committee?
masteryZone.sol: To divide the massive workload of constitution-making. Different committees scrutinized specific aspects (like union powers, state relations, or fundamental rights) and reported to the assembly, streamlining the drafting process.

masteryZone.q: Why was the National Flag adopted on July 22, 1947, before independence?
masteryZone.sol: To ensure that the newly born independent nation had its own sovereign national flag to hoist on the first Independence Day (August 15, 1947) and represent India globally.

masteryZone.q: Why did the calligrapher Prem Behari Narain Raizada request to put his name on every page?
masteryZone.sol: He refused any monetary fee for calligraphing the Constitution. Instead, his sole request to Prime Minister Nehru was to write his name on every page and his grandfather's name alongside his own on the last page, as a mark of family honor.

masteryZone.q: How was the artwork in the original constitution page created?
masteryZone.sol: Artists from Shantiniketan led by Nandlal Bose hand-painted borders, historical murals, and illustrations reflecting Indian history from the Indus Valley Civilization to the freedom struggle on each page.

masteryZone.q: How did the Constituent Assembly handle the transition to a regular parliament after 1950?
masteryZone.sol: Under temporary constitutional provisions, the assembly did not dissolve but transformed into the Provisional Parliament of India on January 26, 1950, passing ordinary laws until the first general elections in 1951-52.

masteryZone.q: How did the Drafting Committee process the reports of other committees?
masteryZone.sol: The Drafting Committee chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar scrutinized the recommendations of the various committees, prepared the first draft, published it for public feedback, and then piloted the draft through clause-by-clause debates in the assembly.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Advisory Committee chaired by Sardar Patel had several sub-committees. Why were separate sub-committees formed for Fundamental Rights and Minorities respectively?
masteryZone.sol: Because although related, the two subjects required distinct expertise. Fundamental Rights dealt with individual liberties against the state (chaired by J.B. Kripalani), while Minorities dealt with community safeguards, political representation, and cultural rights (chaired by H.C. Mookerjee).

masteryZone.q: Case Study: When Prem Behari Narain Raizada calligraphed the English manuscript, he used a special set of nibs. Why was his contribution critical for the preservation of the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Raizada calligraphed the entire text by hand in flowing italic style without any errors. His beautiful calligraphy, combined with the acid-free paper and photolithographic reproduction in Dehradun, ensured a durable, artistic record of India's supreme law.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: On January 24, 1950, the Constituent Assembly gathered for its final session. Members signed three copies of the Constitution. Why were three copies signed instead of one?
masteryZone.sol: To ensure preservation and linguistic representation. Two copies were hand-written (one in English calligraphed by Raizada, one in Hindi calligraphed by Vaidya) and one copy was printed in English. Signing all three validated them as authentic original manuscripts.

masteryZone.q: Explain the role of the major committees in the Constituent Assembly to a junior student.
masteryZone.sol: Major committees acted like specialized project teams. Instead of all 300 members writing the entire constitution together, different groups focused on specific areas (e.g. Nehru on Union powers, Patel on states, Ambedkar on drafting). They did the research, wrote drafts, and presented them to the whole assembly for voting.

masteryZone.q: Explain the timeline of the adoption of India's national symbols by the assembly.
masteryZone.sol:
1. National Flag: Adopted first on July 22, 1947, so it could be hoisted on Independence Day.
2. National Anthem & Song: Adopted on January 24, 1950, to establish them before India became a Republic.
3. First President: Dr. Prasad was elected on January 24, 1950, to assume office on Republic Day (January 26).

masteryZone.q: Explain the post-1950 role of the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: After finishing the Constitution on January 24, 1950, the assembly did not vanish. On Republic Day (January 26, 1950), it became the 'Provisional Parliament' of India. It functioned as India's temporary law-making body until the first general elections were held in 1952 and a newly elected Parliament took over.
